A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sharpness–representation-compression study. Their full text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original training experiments, correlation analyses, and bound-tightness measurements on CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST in Section 4 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds the authors' diagnostic measurements on 181 pretrained vision transformers and variants in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The work continues to analyze existing networks without proposing a new training or inference algorithm. The original LVR, MLS, and NMLS framework remains; residual-network derivations and normalized ViT diagnostics extend theory and evaluation.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST remain. However, v4 omits v3's two-class restriction from Section 4.1 while retaining it for the appendix correlation experiments, and does not identify the ViT evaluation dataset. Changes in dataset or class coverage therefore cannot be established reliably; additional architectures alone do not establish new tasks.

E2.justification: v4 newly evaluates elementwise-adaptive sharpness from Andriushchenko et al. and Kwon et al. against normalized MLS in Figure 4. Petzka et al.'s relative flatness remains in the corresponding appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a distinct protocol for 181 pretrained ViT models, using sigmoid outputs, MSE-based adaptive sharpness, and approximated normalized MLS. Training diagnostics also replace test accuracy with NMLS. The plotted VGG training horizons extend from approximately 500,000 to 750,000 iterations, while the MLP horizons shorten from approximately 1,000,000 to 750,000.

E4.justification: The learning-rate and batch-size sensitivity analyses now include NMLS. v4 additionally reports normalized versus unnormalized ViT behavior and identifies MobileViT/FastViT outlier clusters. Existing bound-tightness, dimensionality, and misclassified-test-sample analyses remain; the test-sample analysis moves to Appendix I.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly specifies Monte Carlo averaging over Gaussian weight perturbations to estimate adaptive sharpness. The original five-initialization averaging and Pearson correlation reporting remain. Perturbation counts and uncertainty estimates for the new measurements are not supplied.

E6.justification: v4 adds the ViT association and outlier findings, reports new NMLS training trajectories, removes the corresponding accuracy curves, and revises other training curves. The MLP MLS-bound scale changes from roughly 50–80 in Figure E.6 to 5–8 in Figure G.7, although its correlation coefficients remain unchanged. Figure 3 largely redisplays existing appendix correlations.

T1.justification: v4 adds a residual-layer telescoping bound in Appendix A and definitions, a lemma, and a proposition connecting elementwise-adaptive sharpness to input-invariant MLS in Appendix E.2. It also corrects the covariance limit by dividing by the perturbation variance and restores the parameter summation and parameter-count factor in the interpolation error bound.

C1.justification: The central sharpness–compression bounds remain the main finding. v4 extends the headline empirical scope to transformers, highlights invariant-sharpness extensions, and explicitly makes generalization secondary to explaining what sharpness measures. NMLS and the earlier invariant-sharpness connection were already present in v3.

C2.justification: v4 adds discussion of vanishing cross-entropy Hessians and loss-function applicability in Section 2, normalization and architecture-specific exceptions in Section 4.3, and data-coverage conditions needed to connect robustness with generalization in Section 5. Earlier dimensionality and held-out-sample interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v4 identifies timm as the pretrained-model source and documents sigmoid outputs, Gaussian perturbation covariance, and gradient-based MLS approximation in Section 4.3 and Appendix F. Appendix J adds a promise to release code after acceptance; the GPU statement is unchanged. ViT evaluation data and approximation budgets remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on SAM/ASAM, classical flat minima, cross-entropy sharpness, and ViT variants, while removing several introductory references on generalization and representations. It explains its relationship to Ma and Ying more explicitly, but retains the same principal theoretical foundations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Existing mathematics is reorganized into explicit definitions, lemmas, and propositions; the covariance discussion moves within Section 3, experimental subsections are reordered, generalization receives a dedicated discussion section, and the held-out analysis moves to Appendix I.

P2.justification: v4 adds the ViT scatter plot and a prominent figure displaying selected existing correlations. Training figures replace accuracy panels with NMLS and revise axes and curves. The bound-tightness figure is enlarged, appendix bound labels become descriptive, and the held-out figure moves from the main text to Appendix I.

improvement.justification: v4 improves mathematical precision through the covariance and interpolation-error corrections, makes the existing bounds easier to follow, and adds useful residual and adaptive-sharpness extensions. Its distinction between compression and generalization is clearer. However, unspecified ViT evaluation data and approximation budgets, plus an unquantified proxy for the formally bounded metric, limit the strength of the additional empirical validation.
